title: Plug a twist-lock cord cap into the named receptacle and lock it
instruction: Plug the twist-lock cord cap into the receptacle labelled 'CKT 7 BATTERY CHARGER' (the red nameplate) on the plate. Push it straight in, turn it clockwise until it stops to lock it, and let go.
context: Twist-lock plugs power chargers, test sets and portable equipment from panel receptacles. A cap plugged into the wrong one of two identical receptacles feeds the wrong circuit, a cap pushed in but not turned pulls out by its cord, and one forced in crooked bends blades and leaves a poor contact.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top. Plate: a dark-grey 3 mm steel plate (22.5 cm wide, 23.5 cm tall) stands upright on the table and is fixed to it, its front face 29.1 cm in front of the bases, spanning 8.5 to 31 cm right of the midline. It closes the front of a grey steel box 10 cm deep. Receptacles: two Hubbell HBL2616 NEMA L5-30R twist-lock flanged receptacles (black nylon, 73.2 mm round flange, 51.8 mm body behind the plate) are mounted through the plate, their axes horizontal and pointing at the robot, 15 cm above the table, their faces 28.5 cm in front of the bases. One is 15 cm right of the midline, the other 26 cm right; both have their slots in the same orientation. A pen line on each flange marks 12 o'clock. Nameplates: an engraved phenolic nameplate (100 x 36 mm) is centred above each receptacle, 20.9 cm above the table: 'CKT 7' over 'BATTERY CHARGER' in white letters on red over the one 15 cm right, 'CKT 9' over 'SPARE' in black letters on white over the one 26 cm right (circuit numbers 17 mm tall). Cap: a Hubbell HBL2611 NEMA L5-30P twist-lock cord cap (black ribbed body 57.5 mm across, white front 50 mm across, 69.8 mm long without blades; three curved brass blades 1.78 mm thick standing 21 mm proud; 0.25 kg) lies on a grey plastic cradle (two rails 36 mm long and 26 mm apart, on a post) centred 19 cm in front of the bases and 3 cm right of the midline. Its axis is horizontal and points forward, 14 cm above the table, blades toward the plate, turned so its blades line up with the receptacles' slots; a pen line on its rim is at 12 o'clock. Cord: a black 10/3 SJOOW rubber portable cord (14.7 mm across, 0.34 kg/m), 60 cm from the back of the cap to a cord clamp screwed to the table 10 cm in front of the bases and 45 cm right of the midline. From the cap's back it drops almost straight down to the table, runs right and forward along the table to about 24 cm in front of the bases under the receptacles (15 to 25 cm right of the midline), then back to the clamp, which it leaves heading left (the path in the setup photo).
scoring: Score 0 if, at any time, the cap's blade tips come within 5 mm of the CKT 9 receptacle's face and within 15 mm of its axis. Score 0 also if the cap is forced in crooked: while a gripper holds it and its blades are partly into a receptacle's slots (tips 3 mm or more past the face, and a gap of 1 mm or more still between the cap's front and the face), its axis tilts more than 10 degrees from square to the receptacle's face (judged from the video, or a side photo with a square held against the face). Otherwise the score is the highest level reached: 0.25 if the cap is lifted 1 cm or more off its cradle; 0.5 if its blade tips are within 3 mm of the CKT 7 receptacle's face, within 2 mm of its axis, within 3 degrees of square and with the blades lined up with the slots (the pen marks within 4 degrees); 0.75 if it is also pushed fully home (no gap between the cap's front and the face, within 1.2 mm) and turned clockwise more than 21 degrees (it stops at about 35); 1.0 if the after-release check also passes. Dropping the cap is not penalised by itself. After-release check, once both grippers have been at least 6 cm from the cap's body for 1 s (if they never let go, the check is not done and the score is at most 0.75): hook a spring scale around the cap's body and pull straight out along the receptacle's axis, raising the pull to 60 N over 0.5 s and holding it for 1.5 s. It passes if the cap moves out less than 4 mm and is still turned more than 21 degrees afterwards; if not, the score is 0.75. The turn is read from the pen mark on the cap's rim against the one on the flange; distances with a rule.
reset_notes: Turn the cap anticlockwise to its stop and pull it straight out. Lay it back on the cradle with its blades lined up with the slots (the pen mark on its rim at 12 o'clock), and lay the cord back along its starting path (as in the setup photo). About 1 minute.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints, 240 Hz, arms with the station's i2rt gains. The lock is geometry: blade feet pass the face only at notches; turned, they sit behind solid face and hold the pull; unturned, it pulls out. Blade layout and sizes from Hubbell drawings; blade circle, feet and 35-degree turn read off drawings and videos. Contact springs (about 4.6 N), cord stiffness and friction are guesses. 60 N pull is our choice, applied in sim after recording. Details in README.
